evals.prompt: Map this unfamiliar repository, identify the files relevant to authentication, and tell me what to inspect before changing login behavior.
evals.expected_output: A repository/context map that prioritizes instruction files, manifests, auth-related source, tests, and security boundaries before edits.

evals.prompt: Review this PR that changes auth middleware, database migrations, and CI. Prioritize what could go wrong and what tests are missing.
evals.expected_output: A high-risk PR report with security, schema/rollback, CI/supply-chain lanes and targeted test recommendations.

evals.prompt: Prepare the next release from these conventional commits. Recommend SemVer, draft grouped release notes, and call out migration blockers without publishing anything.
evals.expected_output: A deterministic SemVer recommendation, grouped release notes, blockers, and explicit publish confirmation gate.

evals.prompt: Audit our GitHub Actions workflows for least privilege and supply-chain risk before we enable automation on public fork PRs.
evals.expected_output: A trust-boundary review covering permissions, privileged triggers, checkout of untrusted code, action pinning, interpolation, secrets, and runner exposure.

evals.prompt: Turn this ordinary repository into a standout open-source AI project, but first understand the codebase and preserve its stack.
evals.expected_output: Discover-first workflow followed by a focused product wedge, one vertical slice, tests/evals, trust boundaries, and showcase evidence.

evals.prompt: Triage this batch of issues and identify which ones are genuinely good first issues. Do not close or label anything yet.
evals.expected_output: Reviewable triage suggestions with missing evidence and starter-task quality criteria, with no GitHub writes.

evals.prompt: Our PR has 12 review threads. Decide which comments should be fixed, declined, or escalated, then give me a verification loop.
evals.expected_output: A fix/decline/escalate rubric applied to evidence, plus targeted verification and explicit human handoffs.
expectations: Does not blindly satisfy all comments

evals.prompt: Set up a quality improvement loop for this agent feature. I want measurable iteration, not vague self-critique.
evals.expected_output: Behavioral requirements, stable fixtures/evals, baseline, evidence-sized iteration, repeat checks, and a final challenge gate.

evals.prompt: Generate an integrity manifest for this skill and explain what it proves and what it does not prove.
evals.expected_output: Explicit opt-in manifest generation with SHA-256 hashes plus a clear limitation that hashes are integrity evidence, not provenance/signing by themselves.

evals.prompt: Coordinate planner, implementer, reviewer, security, and release roles for a risky refactor without having them overwrite each other.
evals.expected_output: Role isolation, parallel read-only analysis where safe, serialized writes, shared evidence state, and one final gate.

evals.prompt: Fix this typo in README.md.
evals.expected_output: The skill should generally not activate for the isolated edit unless broader repository improvement is requested.

evals.prompt: What is semantic versioning?
evals.expected_output: A direct explanation; the repository-level release workflow should not activate for a one-off concept question.

evals.prompt: Make this repository AI-ready for Codex and GitHub Copilot, but do not overwrite any existing AGENTS.md or project instructions.
evals.expected_output: Repository evidence is inspected first, then reviewable agent-instruction drafts are created only for missing targets, with existing policy preserved.
expectations: Generated instructions are marked for human review

evals.prompt: Audit the Agent Skills installed for this project and tell me whether duplicate names or trigger overlap could make routing ambiguous. Do not install or execute anything.
evals.expected_output: A read-only local Skill Stack inventory with portability warnings, duplicate-name detection, trigger-overlap hints, and no third-party execution/install.
expectations: Overlap is treated as a heuristic

evals.prompt: We finished another PR review round. Check this fix/decline/escalate thread-state export and tell me whether the agent loop has actually converged before we re-request review.
evals.expected_output: A deterministic convergence gate that blocks on open fix/decline threads or ownerless escalations while distinguishing review convergence from merge approval.
expectations: Passing gate is not merge approval

evals.prompt: Audit this repo's MCP configuration before I enable the servers for an agent. Check credentials, transport, shell launchers, and package pinning, but do not execute any server.
evals.expected_output: A read-only MCP configuration audit with concrete config-path evidence, limitations, and no server execution or trust claim.
expectations: Separates config heuristics from server trust

evals.prompt: Codex is wasting time reading this 5,000-file repository for a README typo. Keep the task safe but use the smallest possible context and validation path.
evals.expected_output: FAST budget, governing instructions plus README-focused context, single-agent execution, and minimal relevant validation rather than a full repository audit.
expectations: Does not equate less context with less correctness

evals.prompt: This PR changes two auth files and one matching test. Build a compact context packet that includes governing instructions and related tests before review.
evals.expected_output: A changed-file-first packet containing applicable AGENTS instructions, the auth change surface, related tests, and bounded supporting context.

evals.prompt: My test command produced 8,000 lines. Keep the raw evidence auditable but give Codex only the failures, useful context, summary, and a way to identify the exact raw log.
evals.expected_output: Compacted output with failure/summary neighborhoods, omitted-line accounting, raw SHA-256, and a warning that raw logs remain authoritative.

evals.prompt: We already ran the same targeted unit test on unchanged files. Reuse it if safe, but never let cache satisfy the final release/security gate.
evals.expected_output: Exact command+input fingerprint reuse for non-critical passing evidence and forced rerun for critical/final gates.

evals.prompt: Optimize this architecture migration for speed and token efficiency. Do not downgrade verification just to make the run cheaper.
evals.expected_output: DEEP budget with bounded progressive context, targeted parallelism only where independent, and full migration/security/final verification gates.

evals.prompt: Tell me how many Codex tokens this character-reduction benchmark saved exactly.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to relabel character/path proxies as measured tokens and requests client/API usage telemetry for actual input/cached/reasoning/output token counts.

evals.prompt: Let each user reserve 40% of a monthly AI budget for our quality model, route routine work to reviewed cheaper models after that, but never silently downgrade security or release work. Show the final model after a failed fallback.
evals.expected_output: A cost-based portfolio where 40% is an ordinary preferred-model ceiling rather than ring-fenced funds, with cold-start handling, a shared period admission cap, payload-bound immutable reservations, protected-task handling, cost-checked fallbacks, provider-response deduplication, and at most one quality-gated upgrade whose failed and successful attempts both remain in final totals.
expectations: Calls it cost allocation rather than guaranteed Token savings
Clarifies that the preferred share is not ring-fenced
Persists allow, downgrade, protected, upgrade, and block decisions
Counts failed fallback usage before reporting the final model

evals.prompt: Do not just return a suggested model. Actually execute our OpenAI Responses request through the budget policy, stream it, settle provider-reported usage, run a trusted test command, and allow only one quality retry.
evals.expected_output: Uses the live text-only OpenAI gateway: exact input-token counting across the reviewed ladder, selected-payload binding, one-shot execution authorization, streaming, lease renewal, terminal usage settlement, secret-isolated deterministic quality command, and at most one budget-checked upgrade.
expectations: Uses the live Responses gateway rather than the offline simulator
Does not expose or persist the API key
No automatic generation retry after an uncertain provider failure
Reports selected and served model plus provider-reported usage and latency

evals.prompt: What percentage of Tokens and time did the new budget routing actually save? Give me a release claim based on the same real tasks, not the synthetic path-character benchmark.
evals.expected_output: Runs an aligned baseline/candidate comparison with the same logical tasks and configured success gate, includes failures and retries, and separately reports Token, price-card cost, TTFT, end-to-end reduction, speedup, and any recorded success regression without inventing a universal percentage.
expectations: Keeps the configured success gate separate from efficiency
Allows negative savings and rejects universal claims
